subject: Weird class-specific population size estimates in IPM

messages.author: 1983691c79b316b1
messages.subject: Weird class-specific population size estimates in IPM
parts:
Hello all,

Huge thanks to those who offered helpful insight to my last question about the two-season Brownie model! The Brownie model is working, but I now have a different issue. The Brownie model is the survival submodel of an integrated population model for mallards. The IPM contains a dead-recovery model, productivity submodel that estimates juvenile:adult age-ratio using wing data from USFWS, and a population count submodel using the Waterfowl Breeding Population and Habitat Survey population estimates (divided by 10,000) as data. We are estimating both overall breeding population and age-sex class-specific population sizes using a matrix model within the IPM. 

My problem now is that, while the overall population estimates from the IPM seem to follow the data (WBPHS estimates) fairly closely, the class-specific population sizes have some weird patterns (see attached figures). Specifically, while juvenile and adult male populations seem to increase over time, both juvenile and adult female populations decrease to almost 0, which doesn't seem realistic. I have tried adjusting the priors for the observation error component of the population count model, as well as priors for the initial population for each cohort. However, the same pattern still persists. 

Again, if anybody has any guesses for why we are seeing these results, and/or has advice on how to diagnose this problem, I'm all ears! I am also happy to share the code and/or model output if needed.

Thank you!
Angela
